bull.b: The exclusive option broadens Tempest’s in vivo CAR-T opportunity beyond its existing programs and adds access to a clinical-stage candidate. Early evidence of CAR-T generation, expansion, and an initial safety profile could strengthen the pipeline if development and licensing decisions progress.

The Senlang partnership gives Tempest access to clinical development infrastructure and CAR-T expertise while preserving global intellectual-property rights and trial-data access. That structure may improve execution capacity and support future partnering across oncology and autoimmune indications.

Adding an experienced finance leader to the board and appointing a new CFO strengthens financial reporting and audit oversight during an important development stage. Improved governance infrastructure can support compliance, financing execution, and more disciplined corporate decision-making.

bear.b: Tempest has no operating revenue to offset research and development spending, while its latest trailing-period loss remains substantial. Without commercialization or partnering income, financial progress depends on clinical advancement and future funding rather than demonstrated operating leverage.

Ongoing cash outflows require continued access to financing, while negative stockholders’ equity reduces balance-sheet flexibility. Together, these conditions can constrain investment in programs and increase the company’s dependence on external capital to sustain operations.

The equity facility improves access to capital but permits substantial future share issuance over its term, creating dilution risk for existing holders. Reliance on equity funding is particularly material while the company remains pre-revenue and continues to generate negative cash flow.
